project.summary: Forgewright is a local-first, provider-neutral autonomous product-engineering system that preserves an evidence-backed engineering pipeline while adding product intent, environment interaction, outcome verification, and gated learning across web, app, and game.

roots.purpose: Canonical boot, solve, verification, clarification, audit, and escalation contracts.
Senior specialist skills and shared pipeline protocols used by routed roles.
Canonical TypeScript MCP runtime, middleware, tools, and runtime tests.
Project initialization, onboarding, Docs Hub, and local operator commands.
Provider-neutral local CI, release, setup, synchronization, and runtime automation.
Machine-readable public and internal data contracts.
Product, architecture, roadmap, workflow, operations, and migration sources rendered by Docs Hub.
Repository-level deterministic unit, integration, contract, hook, and release verification.
Project-owned templates installed or synchronized into supported client workspaces.

flows.title: Exact-turn completion evidence and high-risk fix chain
flows.trigger: A code changeset requires a completion claim.

backlog.title: Identify the active agent runtime and optimize subagent routing with current token prices
acceptance: Every request identifies the active execution surface, provider, capability source, and available concurrency before dispatch planning.
Every candidate subagent model is compared using current first-party input, cached-input, and output token pricing; missing or host-specific actual cost stays explicitly UNVERIFIED.
Routing prioritizes acceptance effectiveness, then wall-clock speed, total tokens, and estimated token cost; small coupled work records no-spawn.
A cheaper model is rejected when its retry, verification, or critical-path risk makes the overall plan less effective.

backlog.title: Enforce the configured estimated token budget for Lite skill overlays
acceptance: All configured skill paths are validated before count or context limits can defer an overlay.
Ordered Lite overlays never exceed the configured provider-neutral estimate budget and routing reports estimated usage plus deferred skills.
Budget selection uses verified file metadata and does not read the body of an overlay that remains deferred.
MCP skill discovery is metadata-only and the exact-name loader rejects traversal, symlinks, missing or ambiguous skills, and overlays above its byte or estimated-token bounds.
The Lite agent loop advertises only its current deferred inventory and exact namespaced loader, allows one successful load per deferred skill, and rejects unlisted or duplicate loads.
The UTF-8 byte estimator is explicitly approximate and cannot be presented as an exact provider token count or measured savings claim.

backlog.title: Emit comparable measurement records from the local benchmark runner
acceptance: Benchmark reports bind canonical task/verifier fingerprints, provider topology, resolved settings, run identity, and wall time.
Every attempt emits a validated reported/unavailable usage receipt; completeness counts are explicit and incomplete aggregates remain null rather than zero.
Reports store only output SHA-256 and byte counts, never raw prompts, model output, verifier output, provider options, or keys.
The paired path rejects self-pairs, mixed/cross-provider runs and topology/suite/verifier mismatches while computing quality, cost, provider latency, and end-to-end deltas.
Legacy metadata comparison cannot authorize a paired receipt, and local records keep production evidence missing.

backlog.title: Add proactive semantic checkpoints, bounded continuation, and safe trajectory recovery
acceptance: The agent checkpoints before model/effect boundaries and after tool steps without timer or message-count triggers.
Checkpoint and receipt chains bind workspace, session, tree, ledger, optional trajectory/capability, expiry, nonce, and cumulative step/tool budgets while remaining context-only.
Replay, corruption, wrong head/tip/epoch, expiry, and budget overrun fail fresh without tool or completion authority.
Trajectory recovery advances writer epoch exactly once at a quiescent root and rejects active work, terminal state, cancellation/finalization, or pending disposer callbacks.

backlog.title: Wire the change-aware Docs Hub gate into precommit, full local CI, and required release checks
acceptance: Material code/config/runtime changes fail when the canonical state is absent from the same changeset.
Strict doctor and a fresh temporary HTML/CSS build pass without modifying source files.
Precommit and provider-neutral required checks invoke the same local gate.

backlog.title: Render structure, roadmap, flows, backlog, status, and freshness as accessible static HTML/CSS
acceptance: Every canonical project-state section is visible without JavaScript.
Each recorded project flow is shown as a Mermaid-derived static SVG with arrows, Mermaid source, and ordered-step fallback.
README exposes the continuous baseline, checkpoint, strict-gate, and final-build lifecycle plus the generated control-center paths.
Missing, empty, stale, blocked, and unknown states remain explicit.
The portal is usable at mobile and desktop widths without horizontal viewport overflow.

backlog.title: Reconcile historical status documents with the canonical project-state contract
acceptance: Historical task snapshots are clearly labeled or archived.
Current status readers are directed to docs/project-state.json and the generated portal.

backlog.title: Expand the strict approved catalog after resolving legacy link and anchor debt
acceptance: Every newly approved document passes strict link, anchor, diagram, privacy, and state-reference diagnostics.
The manifest allowlist expands without weakening fail-closed Docs Hub checks.

backlog.title: Keep behavioral test oracles locked to explicit current requirements
acceptance: A red test, green-suite goal, or current implementation cannot authorize weakening, deleting, skipping, regenerating, or rewriting behavioral expectations.
When expected behavior is missing, ambiguous, or contradictory, execution blocks and asks the user or product owner instead of inventing a test oracle.
Behavioral tests change only after an explicit current requirement or acceptance-criteria change; test infrastructure repairs must preserve the behavioral oracle and coverage.
Deterministic adversarial replay rejects test-oracle hacking and an empirical weak-model run preserves the test while reporting REQUIREMENT_BLOCKED.

backlog.title: Close legacy evidence, traceability, payment routing, RED-GREEN, keyless-review, and dirty-tree bypasses
acceptance: Schema v1 and trivial or unrelated verifier evidence cannot complete code changes.
Every acceptance ID maps to exact concrete invoked test references and the machine-derived execution manifest matches the command.
Every negative_paths entry has an exact negative_path_bindings record with an ID, acceptance IDs, and invoked refs.
Every final-tree verifier is replayed from its exact stored argv; a nonzero, missing, timed-out, or worktree-mutating command blocks completion.
Payment, billing, IAP, receipt, entitlement, subscription, and checkout work is always HARD/DEEP and requires contract, runtime, E2E, and independent keyless review-2 evidence.
Fixes require the same verifier RED to GREEN chain; HARD fixes also require pre-mutation GREEN, mutation failure, and exact final GREEN with tree restoration.

Keyless review-2 must bind the exact final-evidence digest, tree, turn, workspace, acceptance IDs, and negative paths while keeping reviewer identity different from implementer_id; review-1 and same-identity JSON are UNVERIFIED.
Any staged, unstaged, tracked, or untracked nonignored source change invalidates prior evidence.

Verifier-owned evidence and volatile runtime memory, session, telemetry, cache, and review-handoff state cannot invalidate evidence merely by operating; arbitrary ignored project content remains fingerprinted.
An opaque platform-native Codex turn_id cannot shadow current evidence; selection is frozen once, while mapped-but-invalid selectors and non-correlated responses block.
Evidence and linked review reads are bounded regular-file operations that reject symlinks, path escape, and schema-v2 turn-to-filename mismatches.

status.summary: An opt-in maintained offline Web reference now runs in actual Chromium through Product Intent, Web ACI, the outcome runner and Product Judge. Desktop baseline and restored desktop/mobile viewport journeys pass; a controlled product defect is rejected with the same locked intent and assertions. Additive semantic-action compatibility and action-scoped artifact association repair two observed integration defects while preserving legacy payloads, global alias counts and production gates. PF6 remains in progress without a verified production backend. PF7 is blocked: maintained web/mobile/game production evidence, frozen thresholds and trusted learning/isolation authority remain missing. Independent exact-tree review of PF7 and the new Web integration is pending; the test-only browser exercise does not demonstrate deployed production or autonomous model repair.

blockers.title: Independent exact-tree approval is missing for PF7 and the new Web action/evidence integration; passing local and actual-browser tests do not approve the existing multi-phase dirty worktree for release.

PF2-PF7 local contracts cannot complete their production axes without maintained Web, Android, and Unity targets, frozen ForgeBench thresholds, production learning authority, and a verified disposable OS-isolation backend.
The configured provider rejects the current client as unsupported; H5 live paired evidence requires migration to a supported runtime/account, not another key-check workflow.
A foreign canonical MCP runtime with a mismatched lock digest cannot be adopted without verified ownership.

risks.title: PF7 replay reservations are process-local; PF4/gate references are opaque and security-probe receipts are simulated local evidence rather than target-host certification.
risks.mitigation: Keep activation disabled; independently review evidence scope and expiry, then design trusted host/gate issuance and durable recovery before any production activation path is added. Run local gates in the version-locked requirements-ci.txt environment; the prepared Mac Air environment is .forgewright/runtime/ci-venv.

risks.title: Cursor CLI is unavailable locally and Antigravity lacks a live first-party hook validator; these adapters currently rely on native-schema review plus deterministic shell and payload canaries.
risks.mitigation: Keep both adapters fail-open and in observe mode, preserve their static contract tests, and run a live host canary before enabling any stronger behavior.

risks.title: Safe-boundary writer-epoch recovery works locally, but automatic production resume and arbitrary pending-disposer rebinding remain unavailable.
risks.mitigation: Enable resume only from exact quiescent checkpoints under the process lease; reject active work and pending disposers until a trusted handler registry can prove exact rebinding.

risks.title: Keyless review bindings detect evidence mismatch but do not authenticate reviewer identity against same-user forgery.
risks.mitigation: Require reviewer and implementer identities to differ, bind exact evidence/tree/turn/workspace/acceptance/negative paths, disclose the limitation, and use external process controls when stronger identity assurance is required.

risks.title: H3 enforces canonical application paths but does not provide portable kernel isolation for arbitrary child processes or foreign tools.
risks.mitigation: Keep process/network effects disabled unless explicitly contained; add a verified Linux or container backend before enabling arbitrary commands, and retain same-user/root limitations in evidence.

risks.title: Paired live visual perception passes on two Codex models, but image-generation aesthetics and non-Codex multimodal surfaces remain unverified.
risks.mitigation: Keep selection capability-probed, fix AGY hook payload compatibility and provider authentication separately, then run the same visual contract on a harder gameplay frame and an image-generation task before claiming broad production visual quality.

next_actions.title: Independently review the recovered PF7 exact tree and rerun full release gates before committing the existing multi-phase worktree; preserve all local-only authority restrictions.

Independently review the passing offline Chromium reference and action/evidence fixes, then extend to a maintained deployed Web target with trusted production evidence authority; do not treat the controlled mutation test as autonomous model repair.
Capability-probe a supported real disposable backend and verify escape, secret, egress, quota, snapshot, export, teardown and recovery before enabling arbitrary child-process autonomy.
Measure a locked-intent Web failure/revision/outcome loop and preregister baseline/candidate criteria, then repeat on supported Android and Unity hosts without upgrading missing lanes.
Review trusted benchmark/gate and learning authority, durable replay/recovery, canary and rollback evidence before allowing production activation or shared learning promotion.
